'''Jaroslav Flegr''' (born 12 March 1958) is a Czech [[parasitology|parasitologist]], [[Evolution|evolutionary biologist]], and author of the book [[Frozen Evolution (book)|''Frozen Evolution'']].<ref name=Hall2009>{{Cite journal | title = A review of Frozen Evolution: Or That's Not the Way It is, Mr. Darwin, edited by Jaroslav Flegr | url = http://www3.interscience.wiley.com/journal/121641687/abstract | year = 2009 | author = Hall, B.K. | journal = Evolution & Development | pages = 126–129 | volume = 11 | issue = 1 | access-date = 2009-06-24 | doi = 10.1111/j.1525-142X.2008.00310.x| url-access = subscription }}{{dead link|date=February 2019|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He is professor of [[biology]] at the [[Faculty of Science, Charles University|Faculty of Science]], [[Charles University]] in [[Prague]],<ref>[http://www.natur.cuni.cz/flegr/ Jaroslav Flegr] University website</ref> and is a member of the editorial board of the journal ''Neuroendocrinology Letters''.<ref>[http://www.nel.edu/EditBoard.htm Board of Editors] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090916081239/http://www.nel.edu/EditBoard.htm |date=16 September 2009 }} ''Neuroendocrinology Letters'' website</ref>

His work on how [[toxoplasmosis]]—an infection caused by the [[protozoan]] parasite [[Toxoplasma gondii|''T. gondii'']]—influences [[Personality type|personality]],<ref>{{cite journal |author=Flegr J |title=Effects of Toxoplasma on Human Behavior |journal=Schizophr Bull |volume=33 |issue=3 |pages=757–60 |date=May 2007 |pmid=17218612 |pmc=2526142 |doi=10.1093/schbul/sbl074}}</ref> [[sex ratio]]s,<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Kanková S, Sulc J, Nouzová K, Fajfrlík K, Frynta D, Flegr J |title=Women infected with parasite Toxoplasma have more sons |journal=Naturwissenschaften |volume=94 |issue=2 |pages=122–7 |date=February 2007 |pmid=17028886 |doi=10.1007/s00114-006-0166-2|bibcode=2007NW.....94..122K |s2cid=9610443 }}</ref> and rates of [[traffic accidents]],<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Flegr J, Havlícek J, Kodym P, Malý M, Smahel Z |title=Increased risk of traffic accidents in subjects with latent toxoplasmosis: a retrospective case-control study |journal=BMC Infect. Dis. |volume=2|pages=11 |date=July 2002 |pmid=12095427 |pmc=117239 |doi=10.1186/1471-2334-2-11 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Flegr J, Klose J, Novotná M, Berenreitterová M, Havlícek J |title=Increased incidence of traffic accidents in Toxoplasma-infected military drivers and protective effect RhD molecule revealed by a large-scale prospective cohort study |journal=BMC Infect. Dis. |volume=9|pages=72 |year=2009 |pmid=19470165 |pmc=2692860 |doi=10.1186/1471-2334-9-72 |doi-access=free }}</ref> has received coverage in ''[[The Atlantic]]'',<ref name="Atlantic">McAuliffe, Kathleen (2012). [https://www.theatlantic.com/magazine/archive/2012/03/how-your-cat-is-making-you-crazy/308873/ "How Your Cat Is Making You Crazy."] March issue.</ref> ''[[Salon (website)|Salon]]'',<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.salon.com/2007/03/13/cats_and_gender/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024084537/http://www.salon.com/2007/03/13/cats_and_gender/ |url-status=live |archive-date=24 October 2012 |title=Want a boy? Change the kitty litter |work=[[Salon (website)|Salon]] |author=Catherine Price |access-date=24 June 2009|date=2007-03-13 }}</ref> and ''[[The Guardian]]''.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2003/sep/25/medicineandhealth.thisweekssciencequestions1 |title=Can a parasite carried by cats change your personality? |work=The Guardian |access-date=24 June 2009 | location=London | first=David | last=Adam | date=25 September 2003}}</ref> Flegr maintains that toxoplasmosis might increase the rate of traffic accidents by as much as one million collisions per year.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://news.scotsman.com/uk/Cat-bug--link-to.5332684.jp |title=Cat bug link to 1m crashes |publisher=Scotsman.com |access-date=24 June 2009 |location=Edinburgh |date=4 June 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://praguemonitor.com/2009/05/29/czech-scientists-make-unique-finding-rh-factor-effect |title=Czech scientists make unique finding on Rh factor effect |publisher=Prague Monitor |access-date=24 June 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090607021143/http://praguemonitor.com/2009/05/29/czech-scientists-make-unique-finding-rh-factor-effect |archive-date= 7 June 2009 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/story.asp?storyCode=170964&sectioncode=26 |title=Times Higher Education – Findings: 'Harmless' bug may be killer |publisher=Times Higher Education Supplement |author=Caroline Davis |access-date=24 June 2009|date=2002-08-08 }}</ref> He also believes that ''T. gondii'' contributes to suicides and mental disorders such as [[schizophrenia]].<ref name=Atlantic/>

==''Frozen Evolution''==
[[Frozen Evolution (book)|''Frozen Evolution'']] is a popular science book which aims to explain current developments in evolutionary biology to a wide audience. It also contains [[Infobox|information boxes]] which clarify important topics in science like [[peer review]], [[scientific journal]]s, [[citation impact|citation metrics]], [[philosophy of science]], [[paradigm shift]]s, and [[Occam's razor]]. Flegr's previous research in [[toxoplasmosis]] is also mentioned. 

The book also discusses Flegr's model of frozen [[Phenotypic plasticity|plasticity]], a hypothesis that describes a possible mechanism for the origin of [[adaptation|adaptive traits]]. This hypothesis proposes that [[natural selection]] can only explain adaptation in limited conditions, for example when populations are genetically homogeneous. He describes frozen plasticity as being more general, and maintains that it better explains the origin of adaptive traits in genetically heterogeneous populations of sexual reproducing organisms.<ref>Flegr, Jaroslav (1999). [https://books.google.com/books?id=oWNPNQAACAAJ ''Frozen Evolution: Or, That's Not the Way It Is, Mr. Darwin–Farewell to Selfish Gene''.] CIP Press (English translation).</ref> His hypothesis of frozen plasticity is an extension of [[Niles Eldredge]] and [[Stephen Jay Gould]]'s theory of [[punctuated equilibria]],<ref>Flegr, Jaroslav (1999). [https://books.google.com/books?id=oWNPNQAACAAJ ''Frozen Evolution''], pp. 141–146, 149–156.</ref> which describes the history of most [[fossil]] species as being relatively stable for millions of years, later punctuated by swift periods of evolutionary change during [[speciation]].
